```{r annotate_definitions}
  "te_lfc",
    "WARNING: this is the siCTRL hypoxia-vs-normoxia 1hr contrast (translation_categories_1hr.csv), NOT an si3d knockdown contrast. Never read it as the eIF3d TE change."
)

definitions <- definitions %>% filter(feature %in% annotation$feature)
annotation <- annotation %>%
  rows_update(definitions, by = "feature", unmatched = "error")

# Every tco_struct_* column is region-isolated RNAplfold (-W 150 -L 100), NOT the
# collaborator's whole-transcript fold. The tco_ prefix is what keeps the two apart.
# The RNAplfold parameters DIFFER BY REGION, which neither document said. Verified by
# re-running RNAplfold 2.7.2 on ENST00000000233 and reproducing the stored _lunp files
# bit-for-bit: 5'UTR only under -W 80 -L 40 -u 30, CDS and 3'UTR only under -W 150 -L 100
# -u 30. The annotation previously claimed -W 150 -L 100 for all three, and 01d_'s inline
# docs claimed -W 80 -L 40 -u 30 for all three; each was right about its own region.
#
# CONSEQUENCE: a larger window sees more folding context, so accessibility is NOT comparable
# ACROSS regions - the same caveat the g4 family carries for its differing stride. Compare
# tco_struct_*_utr5 with tco_struct_*_utr5, never with _cds.
struct_params <- function(x) if_else(
  str_detect(x, "_cds(_|$)|_utr3(_|$)"),
  "RNAplfold -W 150 -L 100 -u 30, region folded in ISOLATION; NOT comparable to the 5'UTR columns (different window)",
  "RNAplfold -W 80 -L 40 -u 30, region folded in ISOLATION; NOT comparable to the CDS/3'UTR columns (different window)")

annotation <- annotation %>%
  mutate(definition = if_else(str_starts(feature, "tco_struct_"),
                              struct_params(feature), definition))

cat("Columns carrying an explicit definition:", sum(!is.na(annotation$definition)), "\n")
```

# 3. Annotation integrity

The annotation and the matrix must never drift apart. These are the checks that guarantee
`02_` cannot silently select the wrong columns.

```{r validate_annotation}
stopifnot(
  "annotation does not cover the matrix exactly" =
    setequal(annotation$feature, colnames(features)),
  "annotation has duplicate rows" =
    !any(duplicated(annotation$feature)),
  "a column has no block" =
    all(!is.na(annotation$block)),
  "a column has no family" =
    all(!is.na(annotation$family)),
  "unrecognised block" =
    all(annotation$block %in% c("id", "label", "intrinsic", "external", "eif4e",
                                "technical", "qc")),
  "no family may be assigned 'other'" =
    !any(annotation$family == "other"),
  "unrecognised variant" =
    all(annotation$variant %in% c("single", "current", "corrected")),
  # F6 regression guard: the six _cds/_utr3 columns ending in _mean/_min/_sd were filed under
  # structure_utr5 for as long as the anchor was "$". 18 columns, 6 per region, always.
  "structure families are not 6/6/6 - the region regex is wrong again" =
    identical(as.integer(table(factor(
      annotation$family[str_starts(annotation$feature, "tco_struct_")],
      levels = c("structure_utr5", "structure_cds", "structure_utr3")))),
      c(6L, 6L, 6L)),
  "a deprecated feature is missing from the matrix" =
    all(deprecated_features %in% annotation$feature),
  "unrecognised added_in" =
    all(annotation$added_in %in% c("baseline", "tco"))
)
cat("Annotation integrity: OK\n")

# Leakage guard. What matters is not which block an outcome-derived column lands in, but that
# it is not SELECTABLE - i.e. never in intrinsic/external, the only blocks 02_ draws features
# from. (te_4e_resistance_lfc is outcome-shaped but blocked as eif4e, which is also fine.)
selectable_blocks <- c("intrinsic", "external")
leak <- annotation %>%
  filter(block %in% selectable_blocks,
         str_detect(feature, "^te_|^sig_|^indiv_te_|^delta_te_"))
stopifnot("an outcome-derived column is selectable as a feature" = nrow(leak) == 0)
cat("Leakage guard: no outcome-derived column is selectable\n")
```

## Structural invariants

Every bug the independent audit found was a *class* of bug, not a one-off. These turn each
class into a standing check, so the same shape of error cannot return silently. They run on
the modelled columns only (identifiers, labels and deprecated columns are exempt).

```{r feature_invariants, eval = !params$pass_through}
# Mutations that target the structural invariants themselves.
if (MUT == "duplicate_feature")                       # F4 class
  features$g4mer_mean_cds <- features$g4mer_mean_utr5
if (MUT == "constant_feature")                        # F5 class
  features$proline_fraction <- 0.05
if (MUT == "length_proxy_feature")                    # F2 class
  features$term_interval_codons <- features$utr3_length
if (MUT == "golden_drift")                            # silent per-transcript drift
  features$cds_gc <- features$cds_gc + 1e-6

modelled <- annotation %>%
  filter(block %in% c("intrinsic", "external"), !deprecated) %>% pull(feature)
num_mod <- modelled[map_lgl(modelled, ~ is.numeric(features[[.x]]))]
vals <- features[, num_mod]

# A. No two modelled features may be bit-identical. F4: clip_lee_complete_media_bound was a
#    byte-for-byte copy of clip_lee_glu_dep_bound, and a count summing both double-counted it.
dup_pairs <- list()
for (i in seq_along(num_mod)) for (j in seq_len(i - 1)) {
  if (identical(vals[[i]], vals[[j]])) dup_pairs[[length(dup_pairs) + 1]] <-
    paste(num_mod[j], "==", num_mod[i])
}
cat("A. identical modelled columns:", length(dup_pairs), "\n")
if (length(dup_pairs)) cat("   ", paste(unlist(dup_pairs), collapse = "; "), "\n")

# B. No modelled feature may be constant. F5: three accessibility_*_min columns were
#    identically 0, because min() was taken after NA had been replaced with 0.
sds <- map_dbl(num_mod, ~ stats::sd(features[[.x]], na.rm = TRUE))
const_feats <- num_mod[!is.na(sds) & sds == 0]
cat("B. constant modelled columns:", length(const_feats),
    if (length(const_feats)) paste("-", paste(const_feats, collapse = ", ")) else "", "\n")

# C. Nothing outside the length family may be a near-perfect proxy for a region length.
#    F2: num_structured_regions* was Spearman ~1.000 with its own region length, and its
#    "count" exceeded that length, so length entered the forest three more times in disguise.
len_cols <- intersect(c("utr5_length", "cds_length", "utr3_length", "total_length"),
                      colnames(features))
proxies <- list()
for (f in setdiff(num_mod, len_cols)) {
  if (annotation$family[match(f, annotation$feature)] == "length") next
  for (L in len_cols) {
    ok <- stats::complete.cases(features[[f]], features[[L]])
    if (sum(ok) < 100) next
    r <- suppressWarnings(cor(features[[f]][ok], features[[L]][ok], method = "spearman"))
    if (!is.na(r) && abs(r) > 0.999)
      proxies[[length(proxies) + 1]] <- sprintf("%s ~ %s (rho %.5f)", f, L, r)
  }
}
cat("C. length proxies outside the length family:", length(proxies), "\n")
if (length(proxies)) cat("   ", paste(unlist(proxies), collapse = "; "), "\n")

stopifnot(
  "two modelled features are bit-identical"          = length(dup_pairs) == 0,
  "a modelled feature is constant"                   = length(const_feats) == 0,
  "a non-length feature is a near-perfect length proxy" = length(proxies) == 0
)

# D. Sentinel blocks. A continuous feature where one exact value is shared by a large block of
#    rows is how F1 hid: 1,689 transcripts zero-filled rather than NA, which defeats every
#    NA-based guard downstream. Asserted, with an explicit allowlist - a feature is exempt only
#    by being named here with a reason, never by silently slipping under a threshold.
ZERO_HEAVY_OK <- c(
  "ppp_motif_density"     = "PPP is genuinely absent from ~77% of proteins",
  "g4mer_frac_above_utr5" = "most 5'UTRs have no window above the rG4 threshold",
  "g4mer_frac_above_cds"  = "as above, CDS",
  "g4mer_frac_above_utr3" = "as above, 3'UTR",
  "cnot3_ribo_enrichment" = "-log10 FDR, floored at 0 for non-enriched genes"
)
cat("D. continuous columns where one exact value covers >5% of rows:\n")
sentinel_hits <- character(0)
for (f in num_mod) {
  v <- features[[f]]; v <- v[!is.na(v)]
  if (length(unique(v)) < 100) next                 # not continuous
  tb <- sort(table(v), decreasing = TRUE)
  if (tb[1] / length(v) > 0.05) {
    exempt <- f %in% names(ZERO_HEAVY_OK)
    cat(sprintf("     %-42s value %s in %.1f%% of rows%s\n", f, names(tb)[1],
                100 * tb[1] / length(v),
                if (exempt) paste0("  [expected: ", ZERO_HEAVY_OK[[f]], "]") else "  <- UNEXPECTED"))
    if (!exempt) sentinel_hits <- c(sentinel_hits, f)
  }
}
if (!length(sentinel_hits)) cat("     no unexpected sentinel blocks\n")
stopifnot("an unexplained sentinel block appeared - is a NA being filled with a constant?" =
            length(sentinel_hits) == 0)

# E. Join level. F3 was a transcript-keyed source joined at GENE level, so the transcript we
#    model received a different isoform's value.
#
#    The obvious fingerprint - "a gene-level join is constant within gene" - DOES NOT WORK
#    here, and that is worth stating: this matrix holds exactly one transcript per gene, so
#    there are no sibling isoforms to compare. That is precisely why F3 was silent. A
#    gene-level join does not fail or duplicate; it quietly returns whichever isoform the
#    source happened to carry.
#
#    So the only real check is against the SOURCE, which is possible for the external files
#    this notebook reads itself. Inherited external columns are built in
#    code/predictive_modeling/ and cannot be key-checked from here - see FEATURES.md, whose
#    "assigned in" column names the notebook where each one is built.
stopifnot("the matrix is no longer one transcript per gene - re-derive invariant E" =
            !any(duplicated(features$gene_id_clean)))

occ_check <- features %>%
  dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, stored = hia2026_dhx29_occupancy_tx) %>%
  left_join(dhx29_occ %>% dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean,
                                        src = dhx29_occupancy_score),
            by = "transcript_id_clean")
occ_dev <- max(abs(occ_check$stored - occ_check$src), na.rm = TRUE)
cat("E. hia2026_dhx29_occupancy_tx vs a fresh transcript-level join: max |dev| =",
    signif(occ_dev, 3), ", non-NA", sum(!is.na(occ_check$stored)),
    "(gene-level original had", sum(!is.na(features$hia2026_dhx29_occupancy)), ")\n")
stopifnot(
  "the corrected dhx29 occupancy does not match a transcript-level join" = occ_dev < 1e-12,
  "the corrected dhx29 occupancy has NA where the transcript-level source has a value" =
    !any(is.na(occ_check$stored) & !is.na(occ_check$src))
)
cat("   external columns inherited from predictive_modeling cannot be key-checked here;",
    "FEATURES.md names where each is built\n")
```

## Golden transcripts

A frozen snapshot of 20 transcripts x every modelled feature, committed at
`golden_transcripts.csv`. Range checks pass on a scrambled join and family statistics pass on
a drifted value; this catches "that number is not what it was" whatever the cause. The
transcripts deliberately include the awkward cases: the named spot-check genes, the F1 group
whose structure is NA, truncated CDS and non-AUG starts.

Regenerate **on purpose** with `01d_golden_transcripts.R` when a feature is legitimately
corrected - the commit diff then shows exactly which transcripts and columns moved. A silent
change fails here instead.

```{r golden_transcripts, eval = !params$pass_through}
golden_f <- here("code", "translational_control_overview", "golden_transcripts.csv")
if (!file.exists(golden_f)) {
  cat("No golden file yet - create it with 01d_golden_transcripts.R\n")
} else {
  golden <- read_csv(golden_f, show_col_types = FALSE)
  now <- features %>%
    filter(transcript_id_clean %in% golden$transcript_id_clean) %>%
    dplyr::select(transcript_id_clean, any_of(unique(golden$feature))) %>%
    pivot_longer(-transcript_id_clean, names_to = "feature", values_to = "value_now")

  cmp <- golden %>% left_join(now, by = c("transcript_id_clean", "feature"))
  missing_col <- cmp %>% filter(is.na(value_now) & !is.na(value))
  na_flip     <- cmp %>% filter(!is.na(value_now) & is.na(value))
  moved <- cmp %>% filter(!is.na(value), !is.na(value_now),
                          abs(value - value_now) > 1e-9)

  cat("Golden check:", n_distinct(golden$transcript_id_clean), "transcripts x",
      n_distinct(golden$feature), "features\n")
  cat("  values that moved:", nrow(moved),
      " | became NA:", nrow(missing_col), " | were NA, now present:", nrow(na_flip), "\n")
  if (nrow(moved))
    print(moved %>% arrange(desc(abs(value - value_now))) %>% head(10) %>% as.data.frame())

  stopifnot(
    "a golden feature is missing from the matrix" =
      all(unique(golden$feature) %in% colnames(features)),
    "golden transcript values changed - if this was intended, re-run 01d_golden_transcripts.R" =
      nrow(moved) == 0 && nrow(missing_col) == 0 && nrow(na_flip) == 0
  )
  cat("  golden snapshot matches\n")
}
```

## What `te_lfc` actually is (audit finding F7)

`te_lfc` / `te_padj` / `te_lfc_bin` are **not** an si3d knockdown contrast. They are a
bit-for-bit copy of `output/translation_categories_1hr.csv`, the siCTRL
hypoxia-vs-normoxia 1hr contrast. Two independent signs of it: EIF3D's own `te_lfc` is
**negative** (the documented direction check requires strongly positive under its own
knockdown), and `sig_hypoxia_3d_promotes_TE_1hr_lfc0.5` flags 1,446 transcripts of which only
11 have `te_lfc > 0.5`.

No model is affected - these are `block = label` and `02_` asserts them out of the feature set
- but anything reading `te_lfc` as "the eIF3d TE change" is wrong. The identity is asserted
here so the definition cannot go stale without failing.

```{r verify_te_lfc_provenance, eval = !params$pass_through}
hyp_1hr <- read_csv(here("output", "translation_categories_1hr.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(gene_id_clean = sub("\\..*", "", gene_id)) %>%
  dplyr::select(gene_id_clean, src_te_lfc = te_lfc)

chk <- features %>% dplyr::select(gene_id_clean, te_lfc) %>%
  inner_join(hyp_1hr, by = "gene_id_clean")
ok  <- stats::complete.cases(chk$te_lfc, chk$src_te_lfc)
dev <- max(abs(chk$te_lfc[ok] - chk$src_te_lfc[ok]))
cat("te_lfc vs translation_categories_1hr.csv: max |dev| =", signif(dev, 3),
    ", n =", sum(ok), "\n")
cat("EIF3D own te_lfc:", round(features$te_lfc[features$symbol == "EIF3D"], 3),
    "(negative confirms this is NOT the si3d contrast)\n")
stopifnot(
  "te_lfc is no longer the hypoxia-response contrast - update its definition" = dev < 1e-9
)
```

# 4. Reproduction gate: does the annotation rebuild the baseline 51?

Notebook 07 arrives at its feature set by a regex cascade. This notebook arrives at one by a
block join. They must agree exactly, or `02_` is not modelling the same thing as the baseline.

```{r reproduce_baseline}
baseline_importance <- read_csv(
  here("output", "predictive_modeling",
       paste0("rf_classification_importance_eif33d_promotes_hypoxia_1hr_lfc0.5_",
              "dhx29_kd_feature_clipaggregate_no_boruta_no4e_noOwnTE.csv")),
  show_col_types = FALSE)

# Selection rule, mirroring the baseline run (no4e, noOwnTE, clip aggregate).
aggregate_clip <- c("clip_evidence_count", "clip_eif3_count", "clip_cap_binding_count",
                    "clip_lee_int_stress_lfc", "clip_lee_complete_media_lfc",
                    "clip_lee_glu_dep_lfc", "clip_lee_glu_vs_cm_enrichment")

# The gate reproduces the BASELINE, so it takes the current member of every variant pair.
# The gate reproduces the BASELINE: baseline-era columns only, current variants, and the five
# deprecated positional-CSC features, which the baseline included.
selected <- annotation %>%
  filter(block %in% c("intrinsic", "external"), variant != "corrected",
         added_in == "baseline") %>%
  filter(!(family == "clip" & !feature %in% aggregate_clip)) %>%   # aggregate CLIP mode
  filter(!str_detect(feature, "^(utr5|utr3|cds|total)_length$")) %>%  # log2 versions kept
  pull(feature)

# Sparsity filter is data-dependent, so it is applied on values, not on names.
# 07 computes it on the labelled genes; on this matrix the same 7 columns fall out.
non_na_frac <- map_dbl(selected, ~ mean(!is.na(unlist(features[[.x]]))))
sparse <- selected[non_na_frac < 0.5]
selected <- setdiff(selected, sparse)

cat("Selected by block join:", length(selected), "\n")
cat("Baseline importance CSV:", nrow(baseline_importance), "\n")
cat("Dropped as sparse (<50% non-NA):", length(sparse), "-",
    paste(sparse, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# The frozen baseline CSV predates the tco_struct_* rename, so the gate compares on the
# baseline's spelling. This is a rename and nothing else: the columns, their values and their
# order are untouched, and the count is asserted on both sides.
selected_baseline_names <- sub("^tco_struct_", "struct_", selected)

if (!setequal(selected_baseline_names, baseline_importance$feature)) {
  cat("only in block join:",
      paste(setdiff(selected_baseline_names, baseline_importance$feature), collapse = ", "),
      "\nonly in baseline  :",
      paste(setdiff(baseline_importance$feature, selected_baseline_names), collapse = ", "),
      "\n")
}
stopifnot(
  "the rename changed how many struct columns are selected" =
    sum(str_starts(selected, "tco_struct_")) ==
    sum(str_starts(selected_baseline_names, "struct_")),
  "block join does not reproduce the baseline feature set" =
    setequal(selected_baseline_names, baseline_importance$feature)
)
cat("\nGATE PASSED: the annotation reproduces the baseline 51 features exactly\n")
```

# 5. Write

```{r write_outputs, eval = params$mutate_input == ""}
matrix_out <- features
cat(if (isTRUE(params$pass_through))
      "pass_through = TRUE: baseline copied unchanged\n"
    else
      "pass_through = FALSE: corrected variants added alongside the originals\n")

saveRDS(matrix_out, file.path(out_dir, "feature_matrix_tco.rds"))
write_csv(annotation, file.path(out_dir, "feature_annotation.csv"))

stopifnot("written matrix lost rows" = nrow(matrix_out) == nrow(features))

cat("\nWrote:\n")
cat(" ", file.path(out_dir, "feature_matrix_tco.rds"), "-",
    nrow(matrix_out), "x", ncol(matrix_out), "\n")
cat(" ", file.path(out_dir, "feature_annotation.csv"), "-",
    nrow(annotation), "rows\n")

annotation %>% count(block, name = "columns") %>% arrange(desc(columns)) %>% print()
```

# Summary

The annotation reproduces the baseline feature set exactly by block join, so `02_rf_model.Rmd`
can drop notebook 07's `feature_set` branches without changing what is modelled. `block` makes
the intrinsic-vs-external split a data decision you can revise by editing a CSV, and `family`
is what lets `03_shap.Rmd` sum SHAP over correlated columns exactly.

**State of the build.** Six definitions are corrected (`kozak_pwm_score_v2`, `gc3_internal`,
`cai_internal`, `fop_internal`, `csc_internal`, `tai_gtrnadb`), each kept *alongside* the
column it supersedes so the baseline stays reproducible. The `tco_struct_*` rename is applied.
Five families have been added: `initiation` (Noderer TIS efficiency), `termination` (stop
context + Cridge readthrough), `nascent_peptide`, `polya_track` and `g4` (G4mer, merged from
`output/g4mer/` - no inference re-run).

Every added family must be judged against its own shuffled null via `02b_`/`02c_`, never
against zero: impurity importance is non-negative, so an uninformative family never scores
zero. Of the five, only `g4` clears that floor on AUC, and none beats the no-family arm.

Remaining from `00_`'s inventory: the detectability block
(`control_ribo_frame0_fraction`, `control_ribo_cds_coverage_fraction`), which needs riboseq
coverage rather than a lookup and is deferred.
